cards.text: Here's a song by David, king of Israel, set to the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.' He turns to the rulers: 'Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers?' Then he asks, 'Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?'

cards.question: David just asked the rulers if they speak justly and judge uprightly. What answer does he give?

answers.text: No they devise injustice in their hearts
Yes they judge the people fairly
He leaves the answer up to God

cards.text: And it's not just their hearts: with their hands the rulers mete out violence on the earth. Then David turns to the wicked and the liars.

cards.question: David says the wicked and the liars only start going astray once they grow up.

cards.text: Now David reaches for a picture. Their venom is like a snake's venom, like a cobra, but this cobra has one strange habit.

cards.question: In David's picture, what does the cobra do when the charmer plays his tune?
David compares the wicked to a cobra that won't hear the charmer's tune. What is he saying about them?

cards.text: Friend, that cobra is me when my oven timer beeps mid-batch: ears SHUT. Then the song turns, and David prays straight to God, asking Him to shatter their teeth in their mouths.

cards.question: Next David pictures lions, and he asks the LORD to tame them so they lie down in peace.

cards.text: David keeps praying: may they vanish like water that runs off. GONE. Like a tray of warm cookies in the Millers' kitchen.

cards.question: David asks that when the wicked draw the bow, their arrows will be blunted.

cards.text: Then come two more pictures, and they're heavy ones: a slug that dissolves in its slime, and a woman's stillborn child that never sees the sun.

cards.question: With a slug that dissolves and a child who never sees the sun, David asks that the wicked come to ___

cards.text: Next David pictures pots sitting over a fire of burning thorns, green or dry. Friend, keep your eye on those pots, because this one happens FAST.

cards.question: Before the pots can even feel the burning thorns, green or dry, what happens to the wicked?
Now the song turns to the righteous. David says they will rejoice when they see they are avenged.

cards.text: Then comes a hard, vivid picture. David says the righteous 'will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.'

cards.question: When it's all over, people will say there is surely a ___ for the righteous
David started by asking if the rulers judge uprightly. At the end, people say there is surely someone who judges the earth. Who?

findings.problem: The joke compares the cobra that shuts its ears to the charmer's tune with Papa Dorin ignoring his own oven timer mid-batch. A baker tuning out his own timer doesn't make sense for him, so the comparison doesn't land. The core action in the text is a deliberate refusal to listen to someone trying to reach you, and an oven timer doesn't match that.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The oven-timer joke needs explaining before a stranger gets it: why would a baker shut out his own timer? A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer "He sweeps them away" is the near-exact BSB wording from verse 9. The wrong answers ("They get one last warning" and "They run off and hide") are plain modern phrasing with "They" as the subject. That makes the right answer stand out. Also, "He" has no one it refers to anywhere on the card, because the question never mentions God.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to "the Millers' kitchen." The Millers are never set up earlier in this lesson. The joke logic test only says bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding, and says nothing about whether they know the Millers.
findings.question: Do bakers meet the Millers in onboarding, so Papa Dorin can name "the Millers' kitchen" in a callback without saying who they are? Or does the line need to explain them, the way the drawer's small details need explaining?
